questions.stem: Two siblings need to share a piece of state. The simplest correct fix is:
choices: Lift the state to their nearest common ancestor and pass it down via props
questions.explanation: Lifting state up is the cheapest, lowest-coupling solution. Reach for Context/Redux only when the sharing spans many layers.

questions.stem: Why might a Context Provider cause widespread unnecessary re-renders?
choices: Every consumer re-renders when the value reference changes; passing a new object literal each render does this
Consumers always re-render on every keystroke
questions.explanation: Inline {a, b} as value is a new object each render. Wrap with useMemo so the reference is stable unless inputs change.

questions.stem: Which is the source of truth for a controlled input?
questions.explanation: Controlled means React owns the value. Each keystroke updates state which feeds back as the input's value.

questions.stem: What's the best element for an interactive 'Save' control?
questions.explanation: Buttons are keyboard-focusable, fire on space/enter, and are announced as buttons. Anchors imply navigation.

questions.stem: ARIA attribute aria-describedby is used to:
choices: Link a control to an element that describes it (e.g. an error or help message)
questions.explanation: aria-describedby points to one or more IDs whose contents the AT will announce alongside the control's name and role.

questions.stem: A Redux reducer must be:
choices: Pure — same inputs produce same output, no side effects
questions.explanation: Reducers are deterministic transformations of state. Side effects belong in middleware (thunk, saga) or effects.

questions.stem: Which is the right tool for client-side caching of server data with auto-refetch on focus?
choices: A data-fetching library like TanStack Query or SWR
questions.explanation: Server-state libraries handle cache keys, staleness, refetch, retries, and invalidation — concerns you'd reinvent badly with useState/Redux.

questions.stem: Uncontrolled inputs read their values via:
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled = DOM owns the value. Use a ref to read it when needed, typically on submit.

questions.stem: Which is a sound reason to NOT use Redux?
choices: App is small with localised state and minor sharing — boilerplate cost exceeds benefit
App is large with many cross-cutting actions
questions.explanation: Redux earns its keep at scale. For small apps, useState + Context is simpler and equally correct.

questions.stem: Which is the recommended way to indicate a form input is invalid for accessibility?
choices: Add aria-invalid="true" and link to the error message via aria-describedby
questions.explanation: Programmatic state (aria-invalid) and an associated message (aria-describedby) make the error perceivable to screen readers.

questions.stem: Removing the focus ring with `outline: none` and providing no replacement is:
choices: An accessibility violation — keyboard users lose visual focus indication
questions.explanation: Visible focus is essential for keyboard navigation. Always provide a clear alternative if you suppress the default.

questions.stem: What does `role="alert"` do?
choices: Causes the element's contents to be announced by screen readers immediately when they appear/change
questions.explanation: role="alert" is an implicit aria-live="assertive" region for time-sensitive messages.

questions.stem: WCAG AA minimum contrast for normal-sized body text is:
questions.explanation: Body text must hit 4.5:1 against its background. Large text (18pt or 14pt bold) needs only 3:1. AAA is 7:1.

questions.stem: Why prefer Context over prop-drilling 6+ levels deep?
choices: Maintainability — Context broadcasts to a subtree without each intermediate component needing to know about the prop
questions.explanation: Deep drilling couples every layer to the data shape. Context exposes the value where needed only.

questions.stem: A modal dialog opens. Best a11y practice is to:
choices: Move focus into the dialog, trap focus inside, and restore focus to the trigger on close
Hide the rest of the page with display:none
questions.explanation: Focus management is the heart of accessible modals: enter, trap, restore on close, and Escape to dismiss.

questions.stem: A Context value `{ theme, setTheme }` is recreated each render. Best fix?
choices: Wrap it with useMemo({ theme, setTheme }, [theme, setTheme])
questions.explanation: useMemo on the value object stabilises the reference so consumers don't re-render when nothing they care about changed.

questions.stem: Which is true about `<label htmlFor="email">Email</label><input id="email" />`?
choices: Associates the label so clicking focuses the input AND screen readers announce 'Email' as the input's accessible name
questions.explanation: Labels carry both UX (click-target expansion) and accessibility (accessible name) benefits.

questions.stem: Why is validating on blur often preferred over validating on every keystroke?
choices: It avoids showing errors while the user is still typing and reduces re-render churn
questions.explanation: Mid-typing errors feel hostile. Blur (and submit) signal 'I'm done with this field', when feedback is welcome.

questions.stem: Svelte differs from React in that:
choices: It compiles components to imperative JS at build time with no virtual DOM at runtime
questions.explanation: Svelte shifts work to compile time. The output is small, fast surgical DOM updates without a vDOM diff.

questions.stem: Best place for a 'skip to main content' link?
choices: First focusable element on the page, visible on focus
questions.explanation: Keyboard/screen-reader users tab once and skip past repeated navigation. Visibility on focus is enough.

questions.stem: Which is correct about Vue 3 reactivity?
choices: Proxies wrap reactive state so reads track dependencies and writes notify subscribers
questions.explanation: Vue 3 uses Proxy-based reactivity. Each property read inside an effect registers the dependency.

questions.stem: What problem does React Hook Form solve?
choices: Provides form state, validation, and submission with uncontrolled inputs to minimise re-renders
questions.explanation: RHF registers uncontrolled inputs and only re-renders when needed (errors, watch). Excellent perf for big forms.

questions.stem: A Context Provider re-rendering every input keystroke is best fixed by:
choices: Splitting Context into stable and frequently-changing parts, or memoising the value
questions.explanation: Two contexts (auth, theme) instead of one mega-context limits the blast radius of unrelated updates.

questions.stem: A button with only an icon needs:
choices: An accessible name via aria-label or visually-hidden text
questions.explanation: Screen readers need a text name. aria-label or visually-hidden text inside the button provides it; title alone is unreliable.

questions.stem: Which is correct about Angular vs React on architecture?
choices: Angular is an opinionated full framework (DI, routing, forms, RxJS); React is a view library leaving cross-cutting choices to you
questions.explanation: Angular ships a complete stack and conventions. React picks the rendering battle and lets the ecosystem fill the rest.
